The response's diagnosis of feeling unheard and prescribed statement of need directly follow candidate single-a A3. The closing interprets that challenge as a boundary and prescribes its repetition, matching candidate single-a B4–A5 more closely than the original closing's unsupported shoulder cue. Both versions of single-b support the broader mechanism of reinterpreting literal explanations as emotional evidence; candidate A3/A5 additionally prescribe responses. The transfer need not reproduce its distinct approval-seeking and biscuit tactics. The {prop}, {request}, and {counter} placeholders remain unchanged. Card ID, fingerprint, seed IDs, historical seedBindingHashes, and compiled-pair-draft status are retained; those hashes do not establish binding to the candidate dialogue, which remains an integration step. No bespoke pairs or supporting seeds are supplied, so no particular pair compatibility is established.
